name: AUSCO
aliases: Artificial Urinary Sphincter Clinical Outcomes Trial
question: Do men with primary stress urinary incontinence who receive the AMS 800 artificial urinary sphincter exceed a 65% rate of at least 50% pad-weight reduction at 12 months?

design.population: Men with moderate-to-severe primary stress incontinence from intrinsic sphincteric deficiency (24-hour pad weight at least 100 g) who received a first AMS 800 sphincter at 17 sites in the United States and Australia.
design.description: Prospective multicenter single-arm study with a prespecified performance goal
design.locator: J Urol PMC full text, Methods and Results; journal pp194-202

verdictNote: Performance goal exceeded; single-arm, manufacturer-funded, high-volume surgeons, 12 months of follow-up.
takeaway: In 115 men receiving the AMS 800 artificial urinary sphincter at 17 centers, 94% (91/97 with pad weights) had at least a 50% reduction in 24-hour pad weight at 12 months, exceeding the 65% performance goal; 60% used no pads and 7.8% had a revision.

reports.followUp: 12 months after device activation; 100 participants completed quality-of-life assessments

results.measure: Participants reporting at least 'a little' depressed, baseline versus 12 months
results.note: Within-participant comparison without a control group.

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in 24-hour pad weight at 12 months (available case; goal above 65%)
results.note: One-sided exact binomial test of 65% or less versus above 65%; the sample size of 96 assumed 80% success. Counting the 18 participants without a 12-month pad weight (14 early exit, 4 missed assessment) as failures gave 79% (91/115; 95% CI 71-86%).

results.measure: At least 75% reduction in 24-hour pad weight at 12 months
Mean (SD) 24-hour pad weight, baseline to 12 months, in 97 participants with both measurements
Mean (SD) pads per day, baseline to 12 months, in 101 participants
results.note: Mean difference in pads per day.

Participants satisfied with the device at 12 months
Mean (SD) incontinence events of any type per day by diary, baseline to 12 months, in 95 participants
results.note: Stress events fell from 1.7 to 0.4 per day and urgency events from 1.2 to 0.6 per day.

results.measure: Mean (SD) I-QOL total score, baseline to 12 months, in 100 participants (higher is better)
Mean (SD) IIQ-7 score, baseline to 12 months, in 100 participants (lower is better)
At least 50% pad-weight reduction at 12 months, BMI of 35 or more versus below 30
results.note: Exploratory subgroup comparison; the study was not powered for subgroup differences.

results.measure: At least 50% pad-weight reduction at 12 months, prior radiotherapy versus none

harms.label: Device- or procedure-related adverse event
harms.note: Relatedness adjudicated by an independent medical reviewer.

harms.label: Serious device- or procedure-related adverse event
Any surgical revision
harms.note: Erosion 2 (1.7%), mechanical malfunction 3 (2.6%), lack of efficacy 1, other 4 (pump induration, reservoir herniation, balloon herniation, loose cuff); one revision had two reasons. None for infection.

harms.label: Device deficiency
harms.note: Cuff 8 (7.0%), pump 5 (4.3%), pressure-regulating balloon 4 (3.5%; migration in 2).

harms.label: Postoperative wound infection
harms.note: All resolved without erosion or explantation and were not classed as serious.

harms.label: Deaths during the study period
harms.note: One other serious sepsis case was judged unrelated to the device or procedure.

values.aus: 29% (7/24) at BMI 35 or more versus 11% (6/55) below 30

delivery.label: Sites and enrollment
delivery.value: 17 sites in the United States and Australia; enrollment began October 2019
delivery.note: Participants with prior pelvic radiation were excluded until protocol version C (November 2021).

delivery.label: Prior prostate treatment
delivery.value: 110 of 115 had radical prostatectomy (77 robotic-assisted); 25 (22%) had prostate radiotherapy
delivery.note: Radiotherapy was external beam in 23 and brachytherapy in 2.

delivery.label: Cuff placement and size
delivery.value: Bulbar urethra; 4.0, 4.5 and 5.0 cm cuffs in 30%, 47% and 15%; no 3.5 cm cuffs

delivery.label: Device configuration
delivery.value: All but 2 devices antibiotic impregnated; all pressure-regulating balloons 61-70 cmH2O; 66% placed submuscularly

delivery.label: Activation and follow-up visits
delivery.value: 112 completed activation; 109, 100 and 101 completed the 3-, 6- and 12-month visits

reports.label: Toileting habits and satisfaction
reports.citation: Wood HM, Peterson AC, Breyer BN, et al. How Artificial Urinary Sphincter Impacts Toileting Habits 1 Year After Implantation. *Eur Urol Focus.* 2026;12(2):248-255.

results.measure: Participants with persistent postvoid dribbling at 12 months
results.note: Improved from baseline (p = 0.02) but persisted in most participants.

results.measure: Change in sitting versus standing and urinal versus stall use after implantation

values.aus: Minimal change; not associated with satisfaction

results.note: Pad-weight reduction and ease of device use predicted satisfaction and quality-of-life improvement; limited self-care or mobility predicted more difficulty using the device.

relations.note: MASTER randomized a male sling against the artificial urinary sphincter; AUSCO followed sphincter outcomes in a single arm.
